analysis: What changed vs yesterday: the Anthropic IPO went from single-source WSJ chatter to confirmed fact — priced at $83, above the $70-78 range, 980M shares for $81.3B, the largest IPO on record at roughly a $1.5T valuation — and futures snapped back hard (Nasdaq-100 +1.9%) after five straight S&P down days. That is the whole tape this morning: AI enthusiasm is back in the driver's seat, at least premarket. The counterweight is the Fed: the October minutes landed hawkish (almost all officials see further hikes as likely appropriate, Dec 8-9 decision, ~95-100% priced for a hike, Waller pushing 50bp), and yields are ticking back toward 5.10% on the 10Y. Nvidia is the tell on whether the AI rebound is real or a relief pop: it bounced 2.3% premarket to ~$154.45 but is still ~36% below its Oct 6 high after a record quarter was sold on the margin guide (71-72% for Q4), the leadership transition, and the China/Asia sales overhang. Palo Alto's beat-and-raise plus its $4.5B Applied Compute deal is lifting the whole cybersecurity complex (CRWD +6% premarket), which reads as genuine sector strength rather than index-level noise. Signal vs noise: the confirmed Anthropic pricing, the Fed minutes' hawkishness, and PANW's numbers are signal; the size of the futures pop before the 9:30 AM ET open is noise until it holds through the cash session, and the ANT first trade will likely come well after the bell via Nasdaq's opening auction.

community_signals.takeaway: The 1,007-point, 922-comment Anthropic IPO thread is still the live debate, now reframed by the confirmed $83 price: the split is between 'priced for perfection' skepticism at a ~$1.5T valuation and AI-scarcity enthusiasm. It frames how the market may read ANT's first trade today.
community_signals.title: Anthropic IPO

disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share — above the $70-78 range — selling 980M shares for $81.3B, the largest IPO on record, implying a valuation of about $1.5T. Shares begin trading today on Nasdaq as ANT; options are expected to start Monday, Nov 23.
headlines.why_it_matters: The pricing confirms yesterday's single-source report and is lifting the whole AI trade premarket — a hot debut would be a sentiment tailwind for chips and cloud names; a soft open would revive the week's AI skepticism.

headlines.headline: Futures rebound sharply premarket: Nasdaq-100 +1.9%, S&P 500 +1.1%, Dow +0.6%, as the Anthropic pricing shifts focus away from the AI jitters that drove five straight S&P down days. Prior session: the Dow fell more than 1% for a third straight day (-561 pts to 50,198) while the Nasdaq rose 0.42% to 24,429.
headlines.why_it_matters: A snapback after a five-day slide — breadth into the open will show whether this is a durable turn or a premarket relief pop that fades at 9:30 AM ET.

headlines.headline: Fed October meeting minutes: almost all officials judged further rate hikes would likely be appropriate to return inflation to 2%, with PCE inflation estimated at 3.6% in September. CME FedWatch puts a December hike at roughly 95-100% (94.7% on a quarter point); Governor Waller backs a 50bp move. Next decision Dec 8-9.
headlines.why_it_matters: Hawkish minutes are the rally's headwind — the 10Y is nudging back toward 5.10% and the market is pricing tightening into mid-2027, which caps how far risk can run on AI enthusiasm alone.

headlines.headline: Nvidia bounces premarket: NVDA ~$154.45 (+2.31%) after closing Wed at $150.96 (-2.89%). The Q3 beat still stands — revenue $115.8B (+103% YoY) vs $109.1B expected, adjusted EPS $2.68 vs $2.48, Q4 guide $130B vs ~$125.1B — but the stock is ~36% below its Oct 6 high on the lower 71-72% Q4 margin guide, leadership questions, and Asia-sales uncertainty.
headlines.why_it_matters: The premarket bounce tests whether the post-earnings fade has bottomed — holding above $150 into the open matters more than the bounce itself, given the unresolved China and CEO questions.

headlines.headline: Palo Alto Networks beat and raised: fiscal Q1 revenue $3.44B (+39% YoY) vs $3.31B expected, adjusted EPS $1.05 vs $0.97, full-year revenue guide raised to $14.52-14.57B. It also agreed to buy Applied Compute, an open-weight AI platform, for $4.5B in stock. Shares +9% premarket to ~$371 after already gaining 9.9% in the regular session.
headlines.why_it_matters: A clean beat-and-raise plus a big AI acquisition — the kind of print that lifts a whole sector, and it is doing so premarket.

headlines.headline: Cybersecurity and megacaps ride the rebound: CrowdStrike +6.0% premarket to ~$251.25 on Palo Alto's read-through (it reports Dec 1), and Alphabet +3.9% to ~$293.44. Chip and memory names are also up 3-4.6% premarket (Micron, AMD, Intel, Arm).
headlines.why_it_matters: The move is broad across AI-exposed names, not just the IPO — that breadth is what separates a real risk-on morning from a single-stock story.

Walmart reports before the open (EPS est. $0.64); jobless claims and the Philly Fed survey at 8:30 AM ET — the first data read since the hawkish Fed minutes.
